subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should Gateway pre-upgrade hardening preserve the current origin allowlist as the authoritative decision, or intentionally add a stricter default Fetch Metadata boundary that can reject otherwise allowed browser clients?
rationale: This changes a shipped browser-origin trust boundary and introduces public configuration defaults; code review cannot choose the intended compatibility-versus-hardening policy without owner confirmation.

options.title: Preserve current origin policy
options.body: Use pre-upgrade placement for timing only, let `checkBrowserOrigin` decide allowed origins including loopback aliases, reuse the existing fallback setting, and keep any additional strict header checks explicitly opt-in.

options.title: Adopt a stricter default
options.body: Keep the independent Fetch Metadata rejection only with an explicit compatibility decision, migration guidance, documented exceptions, and real proof across Control UI, WebView, proxy, and native clients.

options.title: Coordinate with related origin work
options.body: Pause this PR until the permanent origin and configuration contract is aligned with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98924.

recommendation.title: Preserve current origin policy
recommendation.body: Use pre-upgrade placement for timing only, let `checkBrowserOrigin` decide allowed origins including loopback aliases, reuse the existing fallback setting, and keep any additional strict header checks explicitly opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion routes the gate placement and flag naming decision to this Gateway security boundary owner.
